iter_evals.query: Search for UK/US legal and self-regulatory sources on influencer marketing disclosure to minors for a YouTube vlog sponsored by Surfshark VPN: FTC Act §5, FTC Endorsement Guides (16 CFR Part 255), FTC .com Disclosures, YouTube paid promotion disclosure rules, UK CAP Code/ASA guidance on “obviously identifiable” ads, affiliate links and discount codes, and direct exhortations such as “use my code” or “try it out.” Include authorities on misleading cybersecurity/privacy and geo-access claims by VPN services (e.g., safety on public Wi‑Fi, malware/data-breach alerts, accessing Netflix libraries or government sites), plus any child-directed advertising standards relevant to whether teen audiences require enhanced ad disclosure or restrictions.

Find applicable advertising/consumer protection rules and guidance for influencer endorsements of VPN/cybersecurity services, especially requirements for clear sponsorship disclosure and substantiation of security/performance claims (e.g., protects you on public Wi‑Fi, encrypts data, alerts malware, data breach alerts, access content/government websites/Netflix libraries by switching IP). Prioritize FTC Endorsement Guides/.com Disclosures and UK ASA/CAP Code or other likely-jurisdiction guidance for YouTube creators and VPN ads.

Find applicable advertising law/guidance for influencer endorsements of VPN/cybersecurity services, focusing on (1) disclosure requirements for sponsored YouTube content, and (2) substantiation limits for claims that a VPN 'keeps you safe online,' 'protects you from public Wi‑Fi,' 'encrypts your data,' 'alerts you to malware/data leaks,' and enables access to region-restricted/government websites or other content. Prioritize UK ASA/CAP Code and CMA influencer guidance, and also FTC Endorsement Guides/.com Disclosures if the channel targets US viewers.
